task: Write one sentence of your own using the word cognizant. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know cognizant should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Good referees stay cognizant of the game clock even while untangling a scuffle at midfield.
Aware is weaker than cognizant — you know a fact exists; cognizant keeps that fact actively in mind while you act.
Watchful is stronger than cognizant: a cognizant person carries a fact in mind, while a watchful one is actively scanning for it moment to moment.

Mindful is the everyday near-twin of cognizant: you keep something in mind as you act — mindful of the ice, you shorten your stride. Cognizant is the formal cousin and adds weight: the awareness comes with responsibility attached, the kind that can be held against you.

Conscious of something means the fact has registered — it has entered your mind. Cognizant goes further: the fact is held actively in mind and weighed in your decisions. You can be conscious of a risk and still never weigh it.

Halfway through the anesthesia rotation, students learn that the monitor is not the patient: a resident must stay cognizant of the drape's rise and fall, the drip's pace, and the surgeon's next request, all while charting the last five minutes.
Cognizant is stronger than plain aware here because the resident is not just informed of these facts — she is holding them actively in mind and letting them steer her hands.
That working awareness, awareness with responsibility attached, is exactly what cognizant names.

Cognizant is boardroom and courtroom English for aware — “the firm was cognizant of the risk.” In everyday speech, aware or mindful sounds more natural; reach for cognizant when the awareness carries responsibility with it.

My flight instructor had one favorite word, and she used it on the first lesson: cognizant.
'Plenty of pilots are aware of their fuel state,' she said.
'They could quote it if you asked.
That is not the same thing.' What she wanted was for the number to sit in the front of my thinking and vote — on the route, on the winds, on whether we turned back early.
Once, when I answered a fuel question correctly but had planned a leg as if the answer didn't matter, she failed the whole flight plan.
'Knowing is storage,' she wrote in the margin.
'You are responsible for what you know.
